title: Tacos al Pastor
intro: Thin slices of chilli-and-pineapple marinated pork, seared hot and tucked into warm corn tortillas with fresh pineapple and onion.
ingredients: 800 g (1¾ lb) boneless pork shoulder, sliced 5 mm thick
3 dried guajillo chillies, stems and seeds removed
2 dried ancho chillies, stems and seeds removed
200 g (1½ cups) fresh pineapple, cut into small chunks
steps: Toast the dried chillies in a dry frying pan for about 30 seconds a side until fragrant, then cover them with hot water and leave to soften for 15 minutes.
Drain the chillies and blend them with the garlic, pineapple juice, vinegar, achiote paste, cumin, oregano and salt until completely smooth.
Coat the pork slices in the marinade, cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat a griddle pan or heavy frying pan over high heat until smoking. Cook the pork slices in batches for 2 to 3 minutes each side until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Sear the pineapple chunks in the same pan for a couple of minutes until lightly caramelised.
Rest the pork briefly, then chop it into small pieces along with any crisp edges.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or directly over a gas flame for a few seconds a side.
Pile pork onto each tortilla, add seared pineapple, chopped onion and coriander, and serve with lime wedges to squeeze over.

title: Guacamole
intro: A chunky, bright avocado dip sharpened with lime and fresh chilli, best eaten the moment it is made.
ingredients: ½ small white onion, finely chopped
1 small tomato, deseeded and finely diced
1 jalapeño or serrano chilli, finely chopped
steps: Halve the avocados, remove the stones and scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Add the lime juice and salt, then mash with a fork until mostly smooth but still with some texture.
Fold through the onion, tomato, chilli and coriander.
Taste and adjust with more salt or lime, then serve straight away with tortilla chips or alongside tacos.

title: Chili con Carne
intro: A slow-simmered pot of spiced beef, tomatoes and kidney beans that tastes even better the next day.
ingredients: 800 g (2 × 14 oz tins) red kidney beans, drained
steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onions, garlic and pepper for about 8 minutes until soft.
Turn the heat up, add the beef and break it apart with a spoon, cooking until it is browned all over and no pink remains.
Stir in the chilli powder, cumin, paprika, oregano and tomato purée and cook for 1 minute so the spices toast in the fat.
Pour in the tomatoes and stock, add the salt and sugar, and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, partly cover and simmer gently for 1 hour, stirring now and then and adding a splash of water if it looks dry.
Add the kidney beans and simmer for a further 20 minutes until the sauce is thick and rich.
Check the seasoning and serve with rice, soured cream, grated cheese or tortilla chips.

title: Chicken Burrito
intro: A big flour tortilla rolled tightly around spiced chicken, rice, black beans, cheese and salsa.
ingredients: 500 g (1 lb 2 oz) boneless chicken thighs, cut into strips
400 g (14 oz tin) black beans, drained and warmed
150 g (1½ cups) grated cheddar or Monterey Jack
steps: Toss the chicken with the oil, cumin, paprika, chilli powder and salt.
Cook the chicken in a hot frying pan over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through, then squeeze over the lime juice.
Warm the tortillas one at a time in a dry pan for about 20 seconds a side so they are soft and pliable.
Lay a tortilla flat and spoon a line of rice across the lower third, leaving a gap at each edge. Top with beans, chicken, cheese, salsa, soured cream and avocado.
Fold the two sides in over the filling, then roll up firmly from the bottom to enclose everything.
Return each burrito to the hot pan seam side down for a minute or two to seal and lightly toast, then cut in half and serve.

title: Chicken Enchiladas
intro: Corn tortillas rolled around shredded chicken, blanketed in a smoky red chilli sauce and baked under melted cheese.
ingredients: 4 dried ancho chillies, stems and seeds removed
2 dried guajillo chillies, stems and seeds removed
1 tbsp vegetable oil, plus extra for the tortillas
200 g (2 cups) grated cheddar or Oaxaca cheese
steps: Toast the dried chillies in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes until soft.
Blend the drained chillies with the tomatoes, onion, garlic, cumin and oregano until smooth.
Heat the oil in a saucepan, pour in the chilli purée and fry it for 3 minutes, stirring. Add the stock and salt and simmer for 15 minutes until thickened to a pouring sauce.
Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Mix the shredded chicken with a ladleful of the sauce and a third of the cheese.
Soften each tortilla for a few seconds in a lightly oiled pan so it rolls without cracking.
Spread a thin layer of sauce over the base of a 23 × 33 cm (9 × 13 in) baking dish. Fill each tortilla with chicken, roll it up and lay it seam side down in the dish.
Pour the remaining sauce over the top, scatter with the rest of the cheese and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until bubbling.
Serve topped with soured cream and coriander.

title: Classic Cheeseburger
intro: A juicy seasoned beef patty with a crisp crust, melted cheese and crunchy pickles in a soft toasted bun.
ingredients: 600 g (1⅓ lb) minced beef, around 20% fat
½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
4 slices American or mild cheddar cheese
steps: Divide the beef into four equal portions and shape each loosely into a patty about 2 cm (¾ in) thick, pressing a shallow dimple into the centre so it stays flat.
Season both sides generously with salt and pepper just before cooking.
Heat a griddle, barbecue or heavy frying pan over high heat. Cook the patties for about 3 to 4 minutes a side for medium, turning only once.
Lay a cheese slice on each patty for the last minute and cover with a lid or bowl so it melts.
Butter the cut sides of the buns and toast them on the hot pan until golden.
Spread mayonnaise on the bottom buns and ketchup on the tops. Layer lettuce, tomato, patty, pickles and onion, close and serve immediately.

title: Mac and Cheese
intro: Macaroni folded into a silky cheddar sauce and baked until golden and crisp on top.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Cook the macaroni in plenty of salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says, then drain.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute to make a paste.
Gradually whisk in the milk, a little at a time, until smooth, then simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until thickened.
Take off the heat and stir in the mustard, nutmeg, most of the cheddar and half the Parmesan until melted. Season with salt and pepper.
Fold the drained pasta into the sauce and tip into a 2 litre (8 cup) baking dish.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the remaining cheddar and Parmesan and scatter over the top.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until bubbling and golden brown on top. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Barbecue Pork Ribs
intro: Spice-rubbed pork ribs cooked low and slow until tender, then glazed with a sticky, smoky barbecue sauce.
ingredients: 2 racks pork baby back ribs, about 2 kg (4½ lb) in total
steps: Peel the thin membrane off the bone side of each rack by lifting a corner with a knife and pulling it away with a paper towel.
Mix the brown sugar, paprika, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper and cayenne and rub it all over the ribs. Leave for 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F). Wrap each rack tightly in foil, place on a baking tray and cook for 2½ hours until the meat pulls easily from the bone.
Meanwhile, simmer the ketchup, vinegar, molasses, Worcestershire sauce and mustard powder in a small pan for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Unwrap the ribs and brush them generously with the sauce.
Grill the ribs over medium-hot coals, or under a hot oven grill, for 8 to 10 minutes, turning and brushing with more sauce, until sticky and lightly charred.
Rest for 5 minutes, slice between the bones and serve with the remaining sauce.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
intro: Buttermilk-soaked chicken pieces in a craggy, well-seasoned crust, fried until deep golden and crisp.
ingredients: 1.5 kg (3⅓ lb) chicken, cut into 8 pieces
2 tsp salt, plus extra for the flour
1.5 litres (6 cups) vegetable oil, for frying
steps: Mix the buttermilk, hot sauce and 2 tsp salt in a large bowl, add the chicken and turn to coat. Cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Whisk the flour, cornflour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, pepper, thyme and 1½ tsp salt together in a wide dish.
Lift the chicken from the buttermilk one piece at a time, letting the excess drip off, and press it firmly into the flour so it picks up a thick, shaggy coating. Set on a rack for 10 minutes.
Pour the oil into a deep, heavy pot to a depth of about 5 cm (2 in) and heat to 165 °C (325 °F).
Fry the chicken in two batches, skin side down first, for 12 to 15 minutes, turning halfway, until deep golden and the thickest part reads 75 °C (165 °F) on a thermometer.
Drain on a wire rack, sprinkle with a little salt and let the oil come back to temperature before frying the second batch.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve hot or at room temperature.

title: Buttermilk Pancakes
intro: Thick, fluffy pancakes with a tangy buttermilk crumb, made for a stack with butter and maple syrup.
ingredients: 45 g (3 tbsp) butter, melted, plus extra for the pan
steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt together in a large bowl.
In a jug, beat the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla together.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and stir just until no dry patches remain; a few lumps are fine. Leave the batter to rest for 5 minutes.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan or griddle over medium heat and brush with a little butter.
Ladle about 80 ml (⅓ cup) batter per pancake into the pan and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until bubbles appear on the surface and the edges look set.
Flip and cook for another 1 to 2 minutes until golden underneath. Keep warm in a low oven while you cook the rest.
Serve stacked with butter and maple syrup.

title: New England Clam Chowder
intro: A thick, creamy chowder of clams, potatoes and bacon that is pure comfort in a bowl.
ingredients: 100 g (3½ oz) smoked streaky bacon, chopped
500 ml (2 cups) clam juice or fish stock
500 g (1 lb 2 oz) waxy potatoes, peeled and diced
400 g (14 oz) tinned chopped clams with their liquid
steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat for 5 minutes until the fat renders and it starts to crisp.
Add the butter, onion and celery and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until soft but not coloured.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute, then gradually stir in the clam juice until smooth.
Add the potatoes, bay leaf and thyme, bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the clams with their liquid and the cream and heat gently for 5 minutes without boiling.
Remove the bay leaf, season well with salt and pepper and serve scattered with parsley and oyster crackers.

title: Caesar Salad
intro: Crisp romaine leaves tossed in a garlicky, lemony dressing with crunchy croutons and shaved Parmesan.
ingredients: 3 thick slices crusty white bread, torn into chunks
120 ml (½ cup) extra virgin olive oil
60 g (⅔ cup) Parmesan, finely grated, plus extra shavings
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Toss the bread with 3 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt and bake on a tray for 10 to 12 minutes until golden and crisp.
Crush the garlic and anchovies, if using, to a paste with a pinch of salt using the side of a knife or a mortar and pestle.
Whisk the paste with the egg yolk, mustard, lemon juice and Worcestershire sauce in a bowl.
Slowly drizzle in the extra virgin olive oil while whisking constantly until the dressing is thick and glossy, then stir in the grated Parmesan and season with pepper.
Tear the lettuce into large pieces, toss with enough dressing to coat every leaf, and add the croutons.
Serve topped with Parmesan shavings and a grind of black pepper.

title: Feijoada
intro: Brazil's beloved black bean stew, rich with smoked sausage and pork and served with rice, greens and orange slices.
ingredients: 500 g (2½ cups) dried black beans, soaked overnight
300 g (10½ oz) smoked pork sausage, sliced
300 g (10½ oz) pork ribs, cut into pieces
200 g (7 oz) smoked bacon or pork belly, cubed
200 g (7 oz) dried or salted beef, soaked and cubed (or stewing beef)
1 orange, halved, plus extra slices to serve
sautéed shredded kale or collard greens, to serve
steps: Drain the soaked beans, put them in a very large pot with the bay leaves and cover with 2 litres (8 cups) of fresh water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 1 hour.
Add the ribs, beef and pork belly to the beans and continue to simmer for another hour, topping up with hot water as needed so the meat stays covered.
In a frying pan, heat the oil and fry the sausage until browned, then set aside. In the same pan, cook the onion and garlic for 8 minutes until soft.
Ladle a cup of beans into the onion pan and mash them in, then scrape everything back into the main pot along with the sausage and the orange halves.
Simmer gently, uncovered, for a final 45 minutes to 1 hour until the beans are creamy, the meat is tender and the liquid has thickened. Remove the orange halves and bay leaves.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve with rice, sautéed greens and fresh orange slices.

title: Ceviche
intro: Cubes of fresh white fish cured in lime juice with chilli and red onion, served ice cold with sweet potato and corn.
ingredients: 600 g (1⅓ lb) very fresh firm white fish fillet such as sea bass, skinned and boned
8 to 10 limes, juiced (about 200 ml / ¾ cup)
1 aji amarillo or red chilli, deseeded and finely chopped
1 corn cob, boiled and cut into rounds
steps: Soak the sliced onion in iced water for 10 minutes to soften its bite, then drain well.
Cut the fish into 2 cm (¾ in) cubes and put them in a glass or ceramic bowl set over a bowl of ice.
Add the salt, garlic and chilli and mix gently, then pour over the lime juice so the fish is just covered.
Leave for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring once, until the outside of the fish turns opaque while the centre stays slightly translucent.
Fold in the drained onion and coriander and taste for salt.
Serve immediately in chilled bowls with the sweet potato and corn alongside, spooning over some of the citrus juices.

title: Beef Empanadas
intro: Golden baked pastry turnovers filled with spiced beef, onion, olives and chopped egg.
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and 1 tsp salt until it looks like coarse crumbs. Beat the egg with the cold water, stir it in and bring together into a smooth dough. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and cook the onions and pepper over medium heat for 10 minutes until very soft.
Add the beef and cook until browned, breaking it up, then stir in the cumin, paprika, chilli flakes and oregano and season well. Cook for 5 more minutes, then cool completely.
Stir the chopped eggs and olives through the cooled filling.
Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Roll the dough out to 3 mm thick and cut out twelve 12 cm (5 in) circles, re-rolling the trimmings.
Place a heaped tablespoon of filling on one half of each circle, brush the edge with water, fold over and press to seal. Crimp the edge by folding it over itself in small pleats.
Arrange on a lined baking tray, brush with beaten egg and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until deep golden. Cool for a few minutes before eating.

title: Arepas
intro: Crisp-shelled, soft-centred corn cakes that are split and stuffed with cheese or whatever filling you like.
ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetable oil, plus extra for cooking
150 g (1½ cups) grated mozzarella or queso fresco, for filling
steps: Stir the salt into the warm water, then gradually mix in the cornmeal with your hand until a soft, smooth dough forms with no dry patches. Add the oil and knead briefly.
Rest the dough for 5 minutes, then divide it into 8 balls and flatten each into a disc about 10 cm (4 in) across and 1.5 cm (⅝ in) thick, smoothing any cracks at the edges.
Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Lightly oil a heavy frying pan and cook the arepas over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes a side until golden with a crisp skin.
Transfer the arepas to a baking tray and finish in the oven for 10 minutes so the insides cook through; they should sound hollow when tapped.
Split each arepa almost in half with a knife, spread with butter and stuff with cheese or your chosen filling while still hot.

title: Jollof Rice
intro: Long-grain rice cooked in a rich, spiced pepper and tomato sauce until every grain is stained red and slightly smoky.
ingredients: 1 scotch bonnet chilli, deseeded for less heat
2 onions, 1 roughly chopped and 1 thinly sliced
100 ml (⅓ cup plus 1 tbsp) vegetable oil
500 g (2½ cups) long-grain parboiled rice, rinsed
steps: Blend the tomatoes, peppers, scotch bonnet and the chopped onion until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot and fry the sliced onion for 5 minutes until golden. Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the blended pepper mixture and add the curry powder, thyme, bay leaves and salt. Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and the oil rises to the surface.
Stir in the rinsed rice so every grain is coated, then add the stock and bring to a boil.
Cover tightly with foil and then the lid, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 30 minutes without lifting the lid.
Check the rice: if it is still firm, sprinkle over a little water, re-cover and cook for another 10 minutes. A lightly caught layer on the base is welcome and adds smoky flavour.
Fluff with a fork, remove the bay leaves and serve with fried plantain or grilled chicken.

title: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
intro: Chicken braised slowly with saffron, ginger and onions, finished with salty green olives and the tang of preserved lemon.
ingredients: 1 preserved lemon, flesh discarded and rind finely sliced
steps: Mix the garlic, ginger, turmeric, cumin, paprika, saffron, 1 tbsp of the oil and some salt and pepper and rub it into the chicken. Leave for 30 minutes or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the remaining oil in a tagine or wide casserole and brown the chicken skin side down for 5 minutes, then turn and brown the other side. Remove to a plate.
Add the onions and cinnamon stick to the pan and cook gently for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Return the chicken to the pan, pour in the stock, cover and simmer gently for 35 to 40 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Add the preserved lemon rind and olives and cook uncovered for 10 more minutes so the sauce reduces a little.
Stir in most of the herbs, check the seasoning, and serve scattered with the rest alongside couscous or bread.

title: Bobotie
intro: A Cape Malay bake of curried minced beef sweetened with fruit and chutney, topped with a savoury egg custard.
steps: Soak the bread in the milk for 10 minutes, then squeeze it out, keeping the milk for the topping, and crumble the bread.
Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onions and garlic for 8 minutes until soft. Stir in the curry powder and turmeric and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beef and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in the squeezed bread, chutney, jam, vinegar, sultanas, apple and salt and cook for 5 minutes. Beat 1 egg and mix it through off the heat.
Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Press the meat mixture into a buttered 2 litre (8 cup) baking dish and smooth the top.
Whisk the reserved milk with the remaining 2 eggs and a pinch of salt, pour it over the meat and push the bay leaves into the surface.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the custard is set and golden. Serve with yellow rice and extra chutney.

title: Jerk Chicken
intro: Chicken marinated in a fiery scotch bonnet, allspice and thyme paste, then grilled until charred and smoky.
ingredients: 1.5 kg (3⅓ lb) chicken thighs and drumsticks, skin on
3 cm (1¼ in) piece fresh ginger, peeled
3 tbsp soy sauce (gluten-free tamari if needed)
steps: Blend the spring onions, scotch bonnets, garlic, ginger, allspice, thyme, cinnamon, nutmeg, sugar, soy sauce, lime juice, oil and salt into a thick, rough paste.
Slash the chicken pieces a couple of times through the skin, rub the marinade all over and into the cuts, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or ideally overnight.
Light a barbecue and let the coals burn down to medium heat, banking them to one side, or heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F).

Grill the chicken over indirect heat with the lid down for 35 to 45 minutes, turning every 10 minutes, until the juices run clear and the thickest part reads 75 °C (165 °F). In the oven, roast on a rack for 40 to 45 minutes.
Move the chicken over the hotter coals, or under a hot grill, for the last 5 minutes to char the skin.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with rice and peas and lime wedges.

title: Poutine
intro: Québec's crisp double-fried chips smothered in hot gravy and squeaky cheese curds.
ingredients: 1 kg (2¼ lb) floury potatoes such as russet, peeled
1.5 litres (6 cups) vegetable oil, for frying
300 g (10½ oz) fresh cheese curds, at room temperature
steps: Cut the potatoes into 1 cm (⅜ in) thick chips and soak them in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and dry thoroughly on a clean towel.

Make the gravy: melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until nut brown. Gradually whisk in both stocks, add the Worcestershire sauce and pepper, and simmer for 10 minutes until thick and glossy. Keep warm.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 150 °C (300 °F). Fry the chips in batches for 5 to 6 minutes until soft and pale, then lift out onto a rack.
Raise the oil temperature to 190 °C (375 °F) and fry the chips again in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain and salt lightly.
Pile the hot chips into bowls, scatter the cheese curds over, then pour the hot gravy over everything so the curds just begin to melt. Serve immediately.

title: Doro Wat
intro: Ethiopia's celebration chicken stew, built on a deep base of slow-cooked onions, spiced butter and berbere.
ingredients: 1.2 kg (2⅔ lb) chicken drumsticks and thighs, skin removed
4 large red onions, very finely chopped
100 g (7 tbsp) niter kibbeh (spiced clarified butter) or ghee
400 ml (1⅔ cups) chicken stock or water
steps: Toss the chicken with the lime juice and a pinch of salt and set aside while you start the sauce.
Put the onions in a large dry pot over medium-low heat and cook, stirring often, for 25 to 30 minutes until they collapse, lose their liquid and turn golden.
Add the spiced butter, garlic and ginger and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the berbere and cardamom and cook for 3 more minutes, stirring so it does not catch.
Stir in the tomato purée, then add the chicken and turn it to coat in the thick onion paste.
Pour in the stock, add the salt, cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is very tender and the sauce is thick and dark red.
Score the hard-boiled eggs lightly and add them to the pot for the last 10 minutes to soak up the sauce.
Check the seasoning and serve with injera to scoop it up.

title: Grilled Cheese Sandwich with Tomato Soup
intro: Golden, buttery toasted sandwiches oozing melted cheese, with a smooth tomato soup for dunking.
ingredients: 800 g (2 × 14 oz tins) whole plum tomatoes
100 ml (⅓ cup plus 1 tbsp) double cream
100 g (1 cup) grated mozzarella or Gruyère
steps: Heat the olive oil in a saucepan and soften the onion and garlic over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, the stock and sugar, bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes.
Blend the soup until smooth, stir in the cream, season with salt and pepper and keep warm over low heat.
Mix the two cheeses together. Butter one side of every bread slice and lay four slices butter side down. Divide the cheese over them and top with the remaining bread, butter side up.
Cook the sandwiches in a frying pan over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes a side, pressing gently with a spatula, until the bread is deep golden and the cheese has fully melted.
Cut the sandwiches in half and serve with bowls of the hot soup.

title: French Omelette
intro: A pale, smooth, softly set omelette rolled into a neat oval around a barely-cooked custardy centre.
ingredients: 1 tbsp finely chopped chives or mixed soft herbs
steps: Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper using a fork until the whites and yolks are fully combined and no streaks remain.
Heat a 20 cm (8 in) non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat and add the butter, swirling until it foams but does not brown.
Pour in the eggs and immediately stir rapidly with a heatproof spatula while shaking the pan, so small soft curds form and the eggs thicken evenly. This takes about 30 to 45 seconds.
When the eggs are mostly set but still glossy and wet on top, stop stirring, spread them level and scatter over the herbs. Cook for 10 seconds more.
Tilt the pan away from you and use the spatula to fold the near edge over the middle, then roll the omelette onto a warm plate seam side down.
Rub the extra butter over the surface for shine and serve straight away.

title: Lamingtons
intro: Squares of light sponge dipped in thin chocolate icing and rolled in desiccated coconut, an Australian tea-time classic.
ingredients: 125 g (½ cup plus 1 tbsp) butter, softened
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a 20 cm (8 in) square tin with baking paper.
Beat the softened butter, caster sugar and vanilla until pale and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour in two additions, alternating with the milk, until the batter is smooth. Spread into the tin and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool the sponge in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack and cool completely. For cleaner cutting, chill it for 30 minutes before cutting into 16 squares.
Sift the icing sugar and cocoa into a bowl and whisk in the melted butter and boiling water to make a thin, pourable icing.
Spread the coconut on a plate. Using two forks, dip each cake square into the icing to coat all sides, let the excess drip off, then roll it in coconut.
Set the lamingtons on a rack for at least 30 minutes until the coating is firm before serving.
